solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient hero or bully?

definitions.meaning: the Trojan champion of Homer's Iliad, slain by Achilles
as a verb, to browbeat or intimidate someone

explanation.surface: A question whether a figure of legend was really just a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the Trojan prince of the Iliad, and a verb meaning to intimidate with bluster.

clue.text: Choice when seconds removed is still a choice

indicators.note: removed takes the letter out

parts.note: a selection is a choice

explanation.surface: A paradox about choosing: lose part of it and it remains a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote is the act of choosing a candidate, a choice by the electorate.

clue.text: Unusually T S Eliot embraced rule for eight-line poems

indicators.note: embraced means the shuffled letters wrap round the abbreviation
unusually says the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: The poet T S Eliot unusually accepted a strict verse form.
explanation.definitionFit: This French fixed form has eight lines with two rhymes and repeated refrains.

clue.text: Ten deer having scampered around edges of Exmoor went in again

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the picked pair
having scampered pictures the letters running about into a new order
edges of picks the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Deer that bolted around the moor went back into the woods. Exmoor is a moorland national park in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having scampered' reworks TENDEER; 'edges of' gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back inside a place is to make a fresh entry, past tense here.

clue.text: Breeze-block providing ventilation

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: a thing providing ventilation

parts.note: a breeze is moving air
a brick is a building block

explanation.surface: A builder's note that a cinder block lets air through.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Breeze-block' looks like one building material, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated brick set into a wall lets outside air circulate under floors, which is its whole purpose.

clue.text: Starry LA mooner confused about Oscar for high-level observer

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the extra letter
confused tells us the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles star who bares their bottom is muddled about an Academy Award.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorary title of the senior British astronomer, a top-ranking stargazer.

clue.text: Terrible mishap covers flaw

indicators.note: the two words cover, or contain, the letters within them

explanation.surface: A dreadful accident hides a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark or defect that spoils something's appearance is a flaw.

clue.text: Needy US soldier turned up, splitting in depression

indicators.note: splitting means the piece breaks into the other

parts.note: a dent is a depression

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A poor American GI appears, falling into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' reads the soldier bottom to top, and 'splitting' breaks that into the depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone poor and in want of basics is needy.

clue.text: Chief element provided by openers to nuclear energy

parts.note: keys open locks
N for nuclear and E for energy

explanation.surface: The vital part supplied by the gateways to atomic power.
explanation.definitionFit: The central wedge stone of an arch, figuratively the principle everything else rests on.

clue.text: Dwelling is rented out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A property is let out to tenants.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, dwelling means living in a place, as a householder who lives on the premises does.

clue.text: Gluttony may be so fatal

definitions.meaning: gluttony is one of the seven sins so named in Christian teaching

explanation.surface: A warning that overeating can kill you.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven cardinal sins, and the same adjective means lethal.

clue.text: Dirk's heel

definitions.meaning: a dirk is a short dagger
a tall thin heel on a woman's shoe

explanation.surface: Seemingly a man called Dirk being a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirk's' reads as a man's name and 'heel' as a scoundrel; really a dagger and a shoe heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a slim stabbing dagger and the tall narrow shoe heel named after it.

clue.text: Shuffle folio papers and secure

parts.note: ID, identity papers
to secure something is to get it

explanation.surface: An office worker shuffles a folder and documents and locks them away.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle is to move restlessly, squirming about in one's seat.

clue.text: Sailor shows disapproval with hard hat

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
boos, jeers
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A seaman jeers at a safety helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard hat' looks like one item, but 'hard' gives H and 'hat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimless felt cap like a fez, traditionally worn by Muslim men, is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Dishevelled bed ruins son's facial hair

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up, so the letters are in disarray

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A messy bed ruins a young man's whiskers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of whisker grown down the sides of the face in front of the ears.

clue.text: Writing materials in Kansas

parts.note: KS is the US postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Pens and paper found in a Midwest state.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured liquids used in pens are among the basic materials for writing.

clue.text: India replacing diamonds with symbol in badges of honour

indicators.note: replacing swaps one letter for a new word

parts.note: the country name is taken as written
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
a sign is a symbol

explanation.surface: Indian medals bear a symbol in place of gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India' looks like the phonetic letter I, but the whole word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblems or badges showing rank or membership, often worn as honours.

clue.text: Cross with dog pound's lock at the front

parts.note: a cross, X, stands for a kiss
a cur is a mongrel dog
L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Someone angry with the dog pound's gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, and 'lock' like a fastening; really a kiss and a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead is a lock at the front.

clue.text: Swelling found in misty eye

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words misty eye, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A lump is spotted on a watery eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed lump on the eyelid is a small swelling.

clue.text: Wild celery is produced in little time

parts.note: small means little
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A wild plant grows quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the wild form of celery, found by the sea.

clue.text: Old codger? Quite the opposite. He's a sweetheart

definitions.meaning: reverse both words of old codger to get a youthful fellow

explanation.surface: Someone protests that an old man is in fact a darling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the opposite of an elderly man, and also an old term for a woman's suitor.

clue.text: Heads of Durham University in new demand for material to go in book

indicators.note: in places the first-letter pair inside the rearranged letters
new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
heads of picks the opening letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: University authorities call for more content in a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DEMAND to ADDENM; 'in' puts DU among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix of extra material added at the end of a published work is just that.

clue.text: See sailor with 6 give up booze

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman
6 refers to the answer of 6 down, a flaw or mark, here a stain

explanation.surface: A seaman with a flaw is told to go teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from alcohol is the narrow sense of refusing to indulge.

clue.text: Stress at home with sibling getting tense

parts.note: in, as in staying in
sis, short for sister
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Domestic strain with a brother or sister making things fraught.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to stress a point and to be emphatic about it mean the same.

clue.text: Run a blog badly, or manage somehow?

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put in a muddled order

explanation.surface: An amateur blogger wonders whether they are just muddling through.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to cope or get on together adequately, without much effort or harmony.

clue.text: In France we almost slip over something sticky

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nous is French for we

indicators.note: over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a tag is a slip of paper, a label

explanation.surface: A traveller in France nearly slips on something tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts NOUS to NOU; 'over' turns TAG into GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of nuts, honey and sugar is famously sticky.

clue.text: Boat parts Royal Mail put in when following cart heading west

indicators.note: following puts the later piece after the cart
in an across entry heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: a dray is a low cart, as used by brewers

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: as, in the sense of while
RM, the initials of the UK postal service

explanation.surface: Post goes in a boat as it trails a westbound wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'heading west' means read right to left; 'put in' places the mail inside the word for 'when', and 'following' sets that after the cart.
explanation.definitionFit: The spars across a mast from which sails hang are parts of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Taking everything into consideration, answer requires Niall to change lines

indicators.note: to change signals that the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: L is line, LL lines

explanation.surface: A reply needs a man called Niall to alter what he says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges NIALL plus LL into LLINALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means all things considered, overall.

clue.text: More than one flock of geese hides around middle of Med

definitions.text: More than one flock of geese

indicators.note: around means the outer word goes round the middle letter

parts.note: animal hides are skins

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Migrating geese take cover around the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wild geese in flight is called a skein, a collective noun, plural here.
